review: Every stanza ends with the same clause pattern (رَابَة/فَاقَ حُبُّهُ + one adjective), so Hebrew repeats רָבָה אַהֲבָתוֹ + the adjective that matches the stanza; only the adjective changes.
3:1 גְּדוּדֵי אוֹיֵב — 'troops of the enemy', the same phrase as גְּדוּדֵי שְׁאוֹל in tr0001; the glossary fixes גְּדוּד for جُنْد.

4:3 יְנַקֶּה הֵד לִבִּי הַסָּבוּךְ — 'He cleanses the echo of my tangled heart', for يَجْلُو صَدَا قَلْبِي الْكَثِيف; הֵד ('echo') is biblical (Job 39:25? הֵד is post-biblical, but the image is required).
5:1–5:2 בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת ... לֹא אִירָא רָע — Psalm 23:4 quoted, because the Arabic وَادِي الْمَوْتِ is itself quoting it.
6:2 לְנַחֲלָה שְׂמֵחָה — 'to a joyful inheritance', for إِرْثٍ سَعِيدٍ; נַחֲלָה is the fixed biblical word for inheritance.
